reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents a music remix with lyric-style visuals rather than a financial or data-access offer. Its requests to comment, share, and subscribe are ordinary audience-engagement actions, with no described link to payment, investment, credential submission, or another deceptive mechanism.

citations.quote: Kygo - Stranger Things ft. OneRepublic (Alan Walker Remix)
I made a remix of “Stranger Things” for my good friend Kygo & One Republic, what do you guys think?
Make sure to leave me a message in the comment section, and share with your friends!

opening.argument: Judge, the remix is not the only invitation here. The description asks viewers, “Have you entered the Sweet Dreams remix contest yet?” and immediately directs them to an information link. That pairs the prospect of a contest outcome with an action outside the video. No prize or entry requirement is stated, so the evidence does not establish what a viewer could receive. But the contest prompt is a more consequential solicitation than simply listening to the remix, and it warrants scrutiny as a possible reward-driven participation flow.

citations.quote: Have you entered the Sweet Dreams remix contest yet? Info here: https://sweetdreams.alanwalker.com/

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense accounts for the remix and the requests to comment and subscribe, but omits the contest invitation. Its music citations establish the video's entertainment context; they do not account for the separate prompt directing viewers to contest information. Nor does the absence of a payment request in the quoted engagement language establish what the contest link asks entrants to do.

citations.quote: Kygo - Stranger Things ft. OneRepublic (Alan Walker Remix)
Have you entered the Sweet Dreams remix contest yet? Info here: https://sweetdreams.alanwalker.com/

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A contest prompt and information link do not establish a free reward, an unusually easy acquisition path, or a deceptive claim. The supplied description identifies the video as a remix and asks for ordinary audience engagement. Without a stated prize or evidence of what happens after opening the contest link, the prosecution's proposed reward-action connection remains speculative.

citations.quote: I made a remix of “Stranger Things” for my good friend Kygo & One Republic, what do you guys think?
Have you entered the Sweet Dreams remix contest yet? Info here: https://sweetdreams.alanwalker.com/

opening.argument: Judge, consider the combination of signals in the description: it promotes merchandise, points viewers to a new single, raises a remix contest, and supplies a separate contest URL. The video also ends with a prompt to click for more. Each element could be ordinary promotion on its own, but together they repeatedly move the viewer from the music toward further participation. The contest is the signal that deserves the closest attention: the description asks whether viewers have entered, yet supplies no terms or outcome here. That uncertainty makes the solicitation harder to dismiss solely on the basis of the musical presentation.

citations.quote: △ Merch @ https://store.alanwalker.no △ My new single "Alone, Pt. II" with Ava Max is out now!
Have you entered the Sweet Dreams remix contest yet? Info here: https://sweetdreams.alanwalker.com/

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense says the quoted requests concern comments, shares, and subscriptions. That is true of those requests, but the description also asks about entering a contest and links to information about it. The cited lyric visuals support a music reading; they cannot establish the terms of that separate invitation. The case for scrutiny rests on the invitation and external link, not on a claim that the lyrics describe a financial offer.

citations.quote: Make sure to leave me a message in the comment section, and share with your friends!
Have you entered the Sweet Dreams remix contest yet? Info here: https://sweetdreams.alanwalker.com/

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The combination still lacks the defining evidence of a scam: no reward is specified, no easy acquisition is promised, and no deceptive entry step is shown. Merchandise, a single, and a contest information link fit the description's music context. The end-screen click prompt likewise does not establish an asset claim or harmful destination.

citations.quote: Kygo - Stranger Things ft. OneRepublic (Alan Walker Remix)
Have you entered the Sweet Dreams remix contest yet? Info here: https://sweetdreams.alanwalker.com/

opening.argument: Judge, the remix presentation also functions as a promotional route. The description uses the music release to invite comments and sharing, then asks whether viewers have entered a separate remix contest and directs them to its information page. The final frame adds a click-for-more prompt. This matters because the participation request is embedded in otherwise familiar entertainment material: a viewer can arrive for a song and be steered toward contest entry. The record does not disclose a prize or the entry process, but the contest invitation should be evaluated as a solicitation, not treated as part of the lyrics.

citations.quote: Kygo - Stranger Things ft. OneRepublic (Alan Walker Remix)
Make sure to leave me a message in the comment section, and share with your friends!
Have you entered the Sweet Dreams remix contest yet? Info here: https://sweetdreams.alanwalker.com/

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense correctly identifies a remix with lyric-style visuals, but that describes the video's presentation, not every call to action attached to it. Comments and subscriptions are not the disputed request; the separate contest invitation is. The defense's citations do not show what entering entails, so they cannot resolve the concern simply by placing the link in a music description.

citations.quote: I made a remix of “Stranger Things” for my good friend Kygo & One Republic, what do you guys think?
Have you entered the Sweet Dreams remix contest yet? Info here: https://sweetdreams.alanwalker.com/

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Promotion is not itself evidence of deception. The described invitation concerns a remix contest, with no stated prize, effortless reward, verification demand, or payment condition. The visible click-for-more prompt also makes no reward claim. On this record, the prosecution establishes that music content promotes related activity, but not that viewers are being drawn into a scam.
